newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen set for renewed uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen set for renewed uptrend.

text.p: Belgian bonds shrugged off a reported sharp fall in German unemployment in March, setting the scene for further gains, traders and analysts said on Monday.
The Bund future initially fell on the report that pan-German unemployment fell 190,000 to 4.48 million in March, but OLO futures rose. The Bund also bounced back to 100.28.

Kredietbank analyst Conrad Fieremans believed the June Bund could fall back to 99.50 on Tuesday if the if the figure was confirmed by Germany's labour ministry. But this would be merely a technical correction before the market resumed its uptrend.
"We are pretty overbought at these levels but underlying sentiment remains good. I think that what we have seen today is only the beginning of a more important upward correction," he added.

Belgian yields collapsed on Monday as upbeat comments on monetary union from European Union finance ministers at the weekend overtook fears of a U.S. rate hike, fuelled last Friday by data showing a strong rise in average hourly earnings.
Belgian money market rates and the Belgian franc, helped by the dollar's rise against the mark, led the way, consolidating the recovery of the last two weeks.
"(The finance ministers meeting) was pretty positive for the whole market...and the Belgian franc has also recovered slightly since Friday," one trader said. "It seems to me a bit more positive."

The benchmark 10-year OLO yield fell to 6.03 from 6.16 percent on Friday. The spread over Bunds -- as is normal in sharp upmoves, when Belgium tends to lag the German market -- edged out slightly to 14 from 13 basis points.
There was some buying of the bonds that will be exchangeable into longer-dated paper at Tuesday's auction, but the main trend was for the curve to flatten, dealers said.

The Treasury is on Tuesday offering OLO 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 10 (8.75 pct, June 2002), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) against OLO 15 (6.75 pct, May 1997) and OLO 8 (9.25 pct, Aug 1997).

"The curve flattened more in Germany than here. That's because we still have some retracement to do on short term rates. We have been a lot flatter than the German curve in the past few weeks," one trader said.
Belgian one week repo rates fell to around 3.20/25 percent on Monday from 3.24/28 late on Friday. Three month Treasury bill yields were around 3.29/33 percent, down from 3.37 percent.
The Belgian franc rose to 20.6315/30 from 20.6363/70 late on Friday.
Traders noted the Belgian yield curve was now almost the same shape as Germany's, with a spread in short term yields of around 20 basis points and in long term yields of 15.
Two weeks ago Belgian money market rates were around 40 basis points over Germany.
